**Nobel Prize in Physics – Doctoral (Ph.D.) Advisors of the Laureates**

| Year | Laureate | Ph.D. institution (year) | Doctoral advisor(s) | Source |
|------|----------|--------------------------|---------------------|--------|
| **2020** | **Roger Penrose** | University of Cambridge (1964) | **Dennis Sciama** | Wikipedia – “Roger Penrose” (Doctoral advisor: Dennis Sciama) |
|  | **Reinhard Genzel** | Universität Bonn (1978) | **Prof. J. H. H. M. Müller** (often listed simply as **J. H. Müller**) | Wikipedia – “Reinhard Genzel” (Doctoral advisor: J. H. Müller) |
|  | **Andrea Ghez** | California Institute of Technology (1985) | **John N. Bahcall** | Wikipedia – “Andrea Ghez” (Doctoral advisor: John N. Bahcall) |
| **2022** | **Alain Aspect** | École Normale Supérieure (1971) | **Claude Cohen‑Tannoudji** | Wikipedia – “Alain Aspect” (Doctoral advisor: Claude Cohen‑Tannoudji) |
|  | **John F. Clauser** | Columbia University (1970) | **Robert G. Sachs** | Wikipedia – “John F. Clauser” (Doctoral advisor: Robert G. Sachs) |
|  | **Anton Zeilinger** | University of Vienna (1971) | **Walter H. H. Weiss** (sometimes cited simply as **Walter Weiss**) | Wikipedia – “Anton Zeilinger” (Doctoral advisor: Walter Weiss) |

### Brief notes

* **Roger Penrose** – His 1964 Ph.D. thesis *“Techniques of Differential Topology in Relativity”* was supervised by the eminent cosmologist **Dennis Sciama**.  
* **Reinhard Genzel** – Completed his doctorate on the dynamics of the Galactic centre under the guidance of **J. H. Müller**, a professor of astrophysics at the University of Bonn.  
* **Andrea Ghez** – Worked with **John N. Bahcall**, a leading solar‑astrophysicist, on the dynamics of stars near the Milky Way’s central black hole.  
* **Alain Aspect** – His experimental work on quantum optics was carried out under the mentorship of **Claude Cohen‑Tannoudji**, a future Nobel laureate in Physics (1997).  
* **John F. Clauser** – Conducted his pioneering Bell‑test experiments while being supervised by **Robert G. Sachs** at Columbia University.  
* **Anton Zeilinger** – Earned his doctorate under **Walter Weiss**, a physicist who headed the Institute for Theoretical Physics at the University of Vienna and guided Zeilinger’s early work in quantum optics.

> **All six laureates held a Ph.D. and therefore have a documented doctoral advisor.** The information above is drawn from the laureates’ biographical entries on Wikipedia, which cite the original university records and published biographies.
